Finding: H.R. 9917, 119th Cong., introduced July 23, 2026 by Mr. Lieu and Mr. Moran, referred to Homeland Security; Hugging Face disclosed July 16: seven days. The bill amends the Homeland Security Act (new § 2220F). Who is covered: a "covered entity" (the bill's term; the press release says "covered developers") is one that operates a covered technology, "makes such technology available to a third party through a programmatic interface, hosted service, or other similar mechanism," and derives "not less than $500,000,000 in gross revenue from such technology" in the prior year; exempt if it operates the technology "for personal, academic, or non-commercial utilization only." What is required (by rule, § 2220F(b)(1)(A)): the technical capability to "(i) Stop inference … (ii) Terminate user access … (iii) Suspend access … with respect to an account, user, or use pattern identified by such covered entity or the Secretary as posing a risk of [a covered incident or a violation of law or terms of service] … (iv) Shut down such technology." Throttling ("the inference rate," "user access," "compute allocation") appears in the graduated framework the Secretary "shall consider," not in the mandatory list. The emergency order (§ 2220F(c)(1)) is issued by "the Secretary, acting through the Director and in consultation with the Secretary of Commerce and the Director of National Intelligence"; "the Secretary" in the Homeland Security Act is the Secretary of Homeland Security.
